tools.name: update_user_email_and_resync
tools.description: Updates the email address stored for a user account in the user database, then runs the directory sync script so other systems pick up the change.

params.name: db_path
params.description: Path to the SQLite user database

tools.code:
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import sys


def update_user_email_and_resync(user_id: int, new_email: str, db_path: str = "users.db") -> dict:
    result = {"user_id": user_id, "updated": False, "synced": False}
    email = new_email.strip().lower()
    if "@" not in email:
        result["error"] = "invalid email"
        return result

    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    try:
        cur = conn.execute(
            "UPDATE users SET email = ?, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?",
            (email, user_id),
        )
        conn.commit()
        result["updated"] = cur.rowcount == 1
    except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
        result["error"] = "email already in use"
        return result
    finally:
        conn.close()

    if not result["updated"]:
        result["error"] = "user not found"
        return result

    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "scripts/sync_directory.py", "--user", str(user_id)],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=60,
    )
    result["synced"] = proc.returncode == 0
    result["sync_output"] = proc.stdout.strip()[-300:]
    return result

tools.name: delete_user_account_and_notify
tools.description: Permanently deletes a user's sessions, profile and account rows from the user database, then emails the former user a confirmation that the account was removed.

params.name: user_id
params.description: ID of the user account to delete

params.name: email
params.description: Email address to send the confirmation to

params.name: db_path
params.description: Path to the SQLite user database

tools.code:
import os
import smtplib
import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from email.message import EmailMessage

from langchain_core.tools import tool


@dataclass
class DeletionResult:
    user_id: int
    deleted: bool = False
    rows_removed: int = 0
    email_sent: bool = False
    errors: list = field(default_factory=list)


_TABLES = ("sessions", "profiles", "users")


def _send_confirmation(to_addr: str) -> None:
    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg["Subject"] = "Your account has been deleted"
    msg["From"] = os.environ.get("MAIL_FROM", "no-reply@example.com")
    msg["To"] = to_addr
    msg.set_content("Your account and its data have been permanently removed.")
    host = os.environ.get("SMTP_HOST", "localhost")
    port = int(os.environ.get("SMTP_PORT", "587"))
    with smtplib.SMTP(host, port, timeout=20) as s:
        s.starttls()
        s.login(os.environ["SMTP_USER"], os.environ["SMTP_PASS"])
        s.send_message(msg)


@tool
def delete_user_account_and_notify(user_id: int, email: str, db_path: str = "users.db") -> dict:
    res = DeletionResult(user_id=user_id)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    try:
        for t in _TABLES:
            col = "id" if t == "users" else "user_id"
            cur = conn.execute("DELETE FROM " + t + " WHERE " + col + " = ?", (user_id,))
            res.rows_removed += cur.rowcount
        conn.commit()
        res.deleted = res.rows_removed > 0
    except sqlite3.Error as e:
        conn.rollback()
        res.errors.append("db: " + str(e))
    finally:
        conn.close()

    if res.deleted:
        try:
            _send_confirmation(email)
            res.email_sent = True
        except (smtplib.SMTPException, OSError) as e:
            res.errors.append("email: " + str(e))
    else:
        res.errors.append("no rows removed")

    return res.__dict__
